text:
Alyssa: quick flag 1_minor but confusing_ on metering page: we say 'requests are billed at the plan rate' which ignores per-token tier attribution we added last quarter. customers keep asking why their dashboard shows split rows.
Marco: can you paste the sentence? I'll propose wording.
Alyssa: current line: 'Usage is billed at the plan rate associated with the API key used.' We should be explicit that billing is computed per-token and any override header can change attribution for parts of a session.
Priya: totally. Analytics team ships attribution annotations per token (header or api-key) so panels can show multiple lines in the same billing window. We should add a tiny example showing a request where 80% tokens are default-tier and 20% are override-tier.
Alyssa: good idea. Draft example I'll add: 
```
# Example attribution (billing window: 2026-06-01)
- API key tier: standard -> 1,200 tokens
- Requests with X-Redwood-Client-Tier: pro -> 300 tokens
Billing: 1,200 tokens at standard rate, 300 tokens at pro overage rate.
```
Marco: small language nit: avoid 'overage rate' unless it's actually priced differently. call it 'override tier rate' to avoid implying credit/threshold logic.
Priya: also note that if a request is routed to a fallback model due to rate-limits, attribution stays with the tier unless the header or api-key changed. Add the line: 'Routing fallbacks do not change billing attribution.'
Alyssa: adding that sentence + a one-line SDK example (node + go) showing the optional header usage. 
Jin: can you use the new header name 'X-Redwood-Client-Tier' and show migration from old 'X-Plan'? Support keeps getting tickets with old header.
Alyssa: yes, will include migration note. Draft node snippet: 
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}`,
    'X-Redwood-Client-Tier': 'pro' // optional: attributes tokens to pro for this request
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'Hello'})
})
```
Draft go snippet: 
```go
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + key)
req.Header.Set("X-Redwood-Client-Tier", "pro") // optional
```
Marco: perfect. One more: add a short note to the dashboard doc explaining how the "tier attribution" breakdown is computed (it's a tag applied at token level, then aggregated by window). Also link to analytics schema.
docs-link-bot: Broken link found: docs/metering.md -> /docs/billing/tiers (404). Suggested replacement: /pricing/tiers.
Alyssa: thanks, I'll update links and add a docs test asserting /pricing/tiers resolves. Priya will you confirm the analytics schema doc path?
Priya: yes path is /analytics/usage-tags. I'll ask infra to add a redirect from old path.
Marco: tiny editorial ask: keep examples concise and avoid full numbers tables; one short bullet example is enough. Also add changelog entry under metering.md: 'Clarified tier attribution and added examples (2026-03-15)'.
Alyssa: added changelog line and pushed PR to review: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/docs/pull/937 - includes copy tweaks, node/go snippets, dashboard caption update, link fix, and a docs-test assert. cc @Marco @Priya
Jin: reviewing now. small nit: in the go snippet, import reference missing bytes pkg in example; add comment 'imports omitted for brevity'.
Marco: LGTM after that tiny fix. :thumbsup:
Priya: approved, leaving a note for infra on redirect.
Alyssa: merging once CI passes. Thanks team! :rocket:
